clue.text: Sheet that's folded into a cone

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a thing, standing for the noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a large size of writing paper
second meaning, split as two words: a jester's or dunce's pointed paper hat

explanation.walkthrough: Split as fool's cap, the word is the cone-shaped dunce's hat; whole, it is the paper size named after the jester's-cap watermark it once bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional large size of writing paper, and a fool's cap is a jester's pointed hat.

clue.text: Plays tricks

blocks.note: first meaning: performs on the violin
second meaning: swindles or cheats, as in falsifying accounts

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it means someone pulls pranks; split, it is two separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is both to play a violin and, informally, to cheat or falsify something dishonestly.

clue.text: Propose to add lines from collection

blocks.note: to propose something is to offer it
taken as written
RY, short for railway, stands for lines; 'add' just tacks it on

explanation.surface: Someone suggests adding a few lines taken from a published collection of poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection' looks like an anthology, but it is the money gathered in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the part of a church service when money is gathered from the congregation, and the money itself.

clue.text: Polish live inside Irish house.

indicators.note: one word sitting inside the other means it is placed within its letters

blocks.note: polish as a noun: a gloss or shine
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A person from Poland is living in a house in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital wants to be the nationality; it is the lower-case shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking house in Ireland, where liquor was sold illicitly.

clue.text: Made a contribution, as initially predicted

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the first letter of as
to bet that something will happen is to predict it

explanation.surface: Someone helped out, just as had been forecast at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, so having abetted means having contributed support to someone's act.

clue.text: Get sent to prison depot

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for being jailed
second meaning: a warehouse, in South and East Asia

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a convict 'goes down' when sentenced; a godown is a warehouse in India and the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for being jailed, and the single word is an Anglo-Indian name for a storage warehouse.

clue.text: Fruit good at first — take again

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the first letter of good
to take on an employee again is to re-engage them

explanation.surface: A fruit was good at first bite, so you go back for another.
explanation.definitionFit: The greengage is a sweet green variety of plum.

clue.text: Man flees from slanderous accusation, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: whatever flees from a word leaves it, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a man is a male
a malediction is a curse or slander spoken against someone

explanation.surface: A man runs away from a defamatory charge, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's style of enunciation, the way they pronounce and choose words.

clue.text: Officer given order to take time at firing-range

blocks.note: WO is a warrant officer
OM is the Order of Merit
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An officer is told to spend some time at the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: Woomera in South Australia is a long-range rocket and weapons testing site.
explanation.definitionFit: The specific place is a famous Australian weapons-testing area, a named example of the general term.

clue.text: Discrimination makes for quarrel

blocks.note: first meaning: a distinction drawn between things
second meaning: a disagreement

explanation.surface: Prejudice leads to people falling out.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a distinction made between things and a dispute between people.

clue.text: Place for shopping basket

blocks.note: first meaning: a co-operative store
second meaning: a wicker cage or basket for poultry

explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British chain of co-operative grocery stores; spelt without the hyphen it is a pen for hens.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooperative shop and the wicker enclosure for chickens share the same letters.

clue.text: Blown up - see the rear falling off

indicators.note: things falling off break apart and land in a jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, its letters also joining the mix

explanation.surface: A photo enlargement shows someone's backside dropping off.
explanation.walkthrough: The word falling does double duty: its letters join the mix as well as the signal 'falling off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blown up is exaggerated or enlarged, bigger than it would be in reality.

clue.text: Collapsed in middle of disco with injury to ears

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter
what reaches the ears is judged by sound, not spelling

blocks.note: the central letter of disco
having an injury is being wounded, said as 'woonded'

explanation.surface: Someone fainted on the dance floor after damaging their hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match is loose: the second part only approximates the spoken word for injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, so someone who swooned has collapsed in a faint.

clue.text: Reach tent after a struggle - make a jump for it

indicators.note: a struggle leaves things disordered, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A camper struggles to get to the tent and then bolts for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a jump for it' sounds like escaping; the jump is the balletic kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap during which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in the air.

clue.text: Always goes too fast at first to contradict

indicators.note: at first says the second idea is put in front of the first

blocks.note: a clock that goes too fast gains time
ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Someone who is always racing ahead from the start tends to contradict people.
explanation.walkthrough: The clock sense of 'gains' is the key; 'aye' meaning ever is poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or speak against, a formal synonym for contradicting.

clue.text: Quickly taking whisky and gin, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be in another form, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: whisky is a spirit
these letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is knocking back whisky and gin in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin, perhaps' tempts you to read gin as another spirit; it is rearranged instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To spirit something away is to carry it off swiftly and secretly.

clue.text: Refuse to attend childbed. I hear (71. 131 Extract information from the French case notes

indicators.note: what the setter hears is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a child is a boy and a small child's bed is a cot; said together they make the word

blocks.clueFragment: (71. 131 Extract information from the French case notes
blocks.note: scanning debris: the enumeration and the following clue, run into this one by the OCR; it plays no part

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sit by a woman's bed during childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned clue runs into the next one; only 'Refuse to attend childbed, I hear' belongs here. Childbed, the old word for labour, splits into a youngster and a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott something is to stay away from it deliberately as a protest.

clue.text: Result of university getting copyright in volume

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside its letters

blocks.note: OU is the Open University
C is the symbol for copyright
a tome is a large book or volume

explanation.surface: A university's research ends up as a copyrighted book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university, abbreviated OU.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end product of something.

clue.text: That's funny — an empty box

indicators.note: a box encloses things, so this word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a carton is a cardboard box
empty is nothing, the letter shaped like zero

explanation.surface: Someone finds it amusing that a box has nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The word box does two jobs: it supplies the outer letters and tells you they enclose the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a comic drawing, something meant to be funny.

clue.text: Extract information from the French case notes

blocks.note: de is French for from or of
a brief is a barrister's summary of the facts of a case

explanation.surface: Someone pulls details out of French police files.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them after a mission to obtain what they learned.

clue.text: Resume progress in such a ferry?

blocks.note: first meaning: carry on driving
second meaning: a ferry that vehicles board under their own power

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as an adjective describing the type of ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to continue a journey, and the hyphenated adjective describes a vehicle ferry.

clue.text: Bundle of sheets causing litter to accumulate in a mass

blocks.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
to roll up, as a snowball gathers bulk

explanation.surface: Bundled paper causes rubbish to pile up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but it is animal bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroll is bedding rolled up for carrying, such as blankets and sheets.

clue.text: Charge soldiers taken in affray

indicators.note: taken in means admitted inside, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: an affray is a public brawl
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are arrested for brawling and face a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an accusation; here it is a load or cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge in the old sense is a load carried, and freight is cargo carried by a vessel or vehicle.

clue.text: Detailed account of these runners given in the round

definitions.text: Detailed account of these runners given in the round

blocks.clueFragment: these runners given in the round
blocks.note: surface reading: a full report on athletes on a circular track
setter's reading: a song sung as a round telling of creatures who ran after a farmer's wife and lost their tails

explanation.walkthrough: A round is a song where voices enter in turn; 'detailed' hints at the tails cut off with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known nursery rhyme is sung as a round and tells how the sightless rodents ran after the farmer's wife.

clue.text: Touched the engine

blocks.note: first meaning: slightly mad, informal
second meaning: a short form of locomotive

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for crazy and also a clipped name for a railway locomotive.

clue.text: Be guided to destination, before impending return

indicators.note: before places the first idea ahead of the second

blocks.note: as a missile homes in on its target
something impending is coming soon

explanation.surface: Someone is steered to their goal ahead of an expected comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A homecoming is an arrival back at one's home, a return.

clue.text: Food and fuel old character accepted

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so it goes within the other word

blocks.note: peat is dug and burnt as fuel
nu is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An elderly person is given food and heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests an elderly eccentric; it is an ancient alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut is an edible seed eaten as a snack, an example of a foodstuff.

clue.text: Exposed to strong sunshine during journey

blocks.note: being in sun or rain is being exposed to it
F is forte, loud or strong in music
sunshine is daylight

explanation.surface: A traveller gets caught in harsh sunlight while on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: In-flight describes what happens aboard an aircraft while it is travelling, such as meals or films.
